correctness.rationale: For each d>=2 and 0<h<1, the proposed axial/transverse axes a,b obey a^2+((d+1)/sqrt d) h a+h^2=1, b^2=a^2+h a sqrt d. A point of the candidate ellipsoid boundary at axial fraction u=|x|/a has exact lens inequality slack h a sqrt d (u-1/sqrt d)^2; strictly positive off the two contact latitudes. After ellipsoid normalization, four signed contact points per transverse basis direction at (±1/sqrt d,±sqrt((d-1)/d)e_j), each weight d/[4(d-1)], sum to zero and have weighted second moment I_d. John’s global contact theorem certifies unique maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoid among all rotations/translations, and unique contacts. Direct quadratic expansion proves dimension scaling h sqrt d→tau with limiting A_tau exp(-tau(A_tau+tau)/2), and fixed-h asymptotic e^-1/2 (1-h^2)^((d+1)/2)/(h sqrt d); monotonicity follows from strict nested lens inclusions and uniqueness. Independent numeric checks in dimensions 2,3,8,23 rederived the exact identity and normalized contact covariance to floating precision, not a proof of continuum.
